You are a senior frontend engineer + product designer (Linear quality). Extend the ROUTINES UI so buyers see and control richer automation: time triggers, chasing, calls, silent shipments, trust levels, proposals, undo and "would handle" hints. Work in the repo directly; do NOT commit or push. A backend engineer implements the API below in parallel (it may not be live yet: build against the contract, handle 404/missing fields gracefully, and test with Playwright page.route mocks). You may edit web/src/components/Routines.tsx, web/src/components/routines/*, web/src/components/DecisionPane.tsx, web/src/components/DecisionList.tsx, web/src/lib/decisions.ts, and add types to web/src/lib/api.ts. Do NOT edit LaunchTimeline.tsx, Header.tsx, App.tsx (unless a one-line mount is unavoidable; then say so), SourceAnchors.tsx, VoiceCall.tsx, EvidenceDrawer.tsx or any Python. A visual redesign (new colours/fonts) may come later: use the existing tokens in web/src/index.css (incl. --color-routine for automation) and keep styles token-based so a re-theme is easy.

Repo /Users/jonasstenglein/OtherProjects/StartMunichHack/ask-soony; React 19, Tailwind v4, lucide-react, no new packages. Read the routines UI first (Routines.tsx, routines/types.ts, FlowGraph.tsx, RoutineFlow.tsx, RoutineCard.tsx) and the main panes (DecisionPane.tsx, DecisionList.tsx, lib/decisions.ts). Live app :8000 (login form /login; password ASK_DASHBOARD_PASSWORD in .env, never print it). Never click Approve/Escalate/Dismiss/Run now/accept on real data (real emails); mock with page.route.

API CONTRACT (additive to the existing routines API):
- Recipe: optional `on`: "decisions" | "waiting" | "shipments" (trigger node text: "Every portal check · open decisions" / "Messages still waiting for an answer" / "Shipments that stopped updating"). New condition fields: hours_left (op lt/gt, number: "less than 2 h before the deadline"), waiting_hours (lt/gt: "no answer for more than 2 h"), has_reply (is yes/no), reply_after_launch (is yes/no), silent_hours (lt/gt). New step kinds: `chase` (follow-up email in the same thread; icon Reply/MailWarning), `call` (phone the responsible person; icon Phone, its own emphasis), `ask_status` (ask a supplier for a shipment's status; icon PackageSearch). Every step/condition has `id` and buyer-readable `text`.
- Routine gets `mode`: "ask" | "tell" | "quiet" (default "tell"); `enabled` stays the on/off switch. POST /api/routines/{id}/mode {mode}.
- GET /api/routines/proposals → {proposals: [{id, routine_id, routine_name, card_id?, shipment_id?, step:{do,text,...}, preview_text, created_at, status:"pending"|"done"|"skipped"}]}; POST /api/routines/proposals/{id}/accept → {ok, result}; POST /api/routines/proposals/{id}/skip.
- POST /api/routines/actions/{action_id}/undo → {ok: true, undone: true} or {ok: false, reason}.
- GET /api/routines/would-handle → {card_id: [{routine_id, routine_name, mode, enabled}]}.
- Activity items (state.activity) carry `via` ("routine: <name>") and decision_status entries (card.ui) may carry reply_date, reply_quantity, reply_after_launch, reply, reply_from; actions in state may have an `id` (if the activity item lacks an action id, hide Undo).

Build:
1. Flow + steps views: render the new trigger texts, condition chips for the numeric/boolean fields in plain words (never field names), new step nodes with icons; the "call" node visually distinct (it reaches a person); the palette gains "Chase once if no answer", "Call me", "Ask for a status". Keep the review-before-apply flow.
2. Trust selector per routine replacing the bare switch semantics: a compact segmented control "Ask me · Do it and tell me · Do it quietly" plus the existing on/off switch; tooltip lines: Ask me = "prepares it, you confirm with one tap"; tell = "does it and tells you"; quiet = "does it, you see it in Handled for you".
3. Proposals: at the top of the Routines sheet "Waiting for your OK · N" with each proposal (routine name, what it would do, preview_text, [Do it] [Skip]); also inside DecisionPane for the selected card: "Your routine ‘…’ suggests: … [Do it] [Skip]". Poll proposals with the existing refresh. Show a count on the Routines tab badge if App/Header already exposes a slot via Routines' button (the Routines component renders its own trigger button: add the count there).
4. Undo: in DecisionList's "Handled for you" rows and in the pane when a routine handled the card: "Undo" → POST undo; on ok:false show the reason inline (e.g. "The email already went out. Send a correction instead?").
5. Would handle: in DecisionPane, when /would-handle lists the selected card: a quiet chip "Your routine ‘…’ would handle this" + "Turn it on" (POST toggle enabled true, and mode tell) / "Let it ask me first" (mode ask).
6. Replies: in DecisionPane show reply facts when present ("Supplier confirms 20,000 on Tue 24 Nov · after launch" in red only if reply_after_launch).
Verify: cd web && npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.app.json && npm run build; screenshots with mocked API at 1440 and 390 under /Users/jonasstenglein/.claude/jobs/3021cc1a/tmp/routines-more/. Final report: what changed, screenshots, anything the lead must wire.

All six parts of the routines UI are built against the contract, nothing is committed or pushed, and the type check and `npm run build` both pass. All screenshots use mocked routines endpoints, since the backend may not be live yet, and the mocks answered every write (Do it, Skip, Undo, mode, toggle), so nothing real was sent. `npm run build` rewrote `web/dist`, which is what the live app on :8000 serves, so the new UI is already showing there.

**What changed**
1. **Flow and steps views:** the trigger node shows the three new trigger texts. Conditions on the new fields read in plain words ("No answer for more than 2 h", "Less than 6 h before the deadline", "The supplier has not answered yet"); a field name never shows. The new steps have their own icons: chase (MailWarning), call (Phone) and ask status (PackageSearch). A call step is purple and marked "Rings a person". The palette gains "Chase once if no answer", "Call me" and "Ask for a status". Changes still go through review before they apply.
2. **Trust selector:** each routine has "Ask me · Do it and tell me · Do it quietly" next to the existing on/off switch, with your three explanation lines as tooltips and as a caption under the control. A change shows straight away and goes back if the server refuses it; a 404 says trust levels are not available yet.
3. **Proposals:** "Waiting for your OK · N" sits at the top of the Routines sheet. Each one shows the routine name, what it would do, the card or shipment and the preview text, with Do it and Skip. The selected card's pane shows "Your routine ‘…’ suggests: …". The Routines button badge now counts proposals plus voice drafts.
4. **Undo:** it appears in the "Handled for you" rows and in the pane when a routine handled the card. If the server says no, its reason replaces the button ("The email already went out. Send a correction instead?"). The list and the pane share the result.
5. **Would handle:** the pane shows a quiet chip, "Your routine ‘…’ would handle this", with "Turn it on" (switches it on in tell mode) and "Let it ask me first" (ask mode).
6. **Replies:** the pane shows a line such as "Hwaseong Memory confirms 20,000 Game Card 128 GB on Tue 24 Nov", with "· after launch" in red only when `reply_after_launch` is true.

App.tsx and the other files on your do-not-touch list are unchanged. The new pieces are in `web/src/components/routines/`: `live.ts` (one shared store for proposals, would-handle and undo results), `Proposals.tsx`, `PaneHints.tsx` and `Undo.tsx`. Proposals and would-handle refresh whenever the app reloads its state (every 5 s), at most every 4 s, plus after each action; a missing endpoint simply counts as empty.

**For the lead and the backend**
- **Undo id:** the UI reads the action id from `action_id` on the activity item, falling back to `id`. Please confirm the field name; without either, Undo stays hidden.
- **Recipe text:** conditions and steps use the recipe's `text` when it is set; the plain-word fallback only covers the new fields.
- **Would-handle shape:** I expect `{card_id: [...]}` at the top level, with no wrapper object.
- **Undo in the list:** DecisionList has no refresh hook, so after an undo there the list waits for the app's next 5 s refresh; it shows "Undone" straight away. Passing an `onChanged` from App would make it instant, but I left App alone.
- **Working tree:** `src/ask_soony/cardtools.py` and `routines.py` show as modified. Those are the backend engineer's changes, not mine.
